newsitem.title: USA: Final phase of Food Lion lawsuit due.
newsitem.headline: Final phase of Food Lion lawsuit due.

text.p: The third and final phase of grocery store chain Food Lion Inc's lawsuit against the ABC television network was due to get underway in federal court on Monday, with jurors hearing evidence on punitive damages, the grocer said.
Food Lion sued ABC and four producers of its newsmagazine show "PrimeTime Live" for a 1992 program that claimed the grocer sold old food and repackaged out-of-date merchandise.

Salisbury, N.C.-based Food Lion charged the ABC producers who worked undercover at two Food Lion stores with fraud, deceptive trade practices, conspiracy and breach of duty of loyalty. It argued that while the producers were employed by the store they were obligated to ensure sanitary practices.

Previously the jury found New York-based ABC, a unit of Walt Disney Co, and its producers had committed fraud, trespass and breach of employee loyalty in the undercover investigation and awarded the grocer $1,402 in actual damages.

Food Lion said it plans to argue for more in punitive damages in federal court in Greensboro, N.C. and will call as an expert witness E. Robert Lissit, an associate professor of broadcast journalism at the S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications at Syracuse University in New York.
